 (BY SHRI A.R.BEN - DY. G.A FOR RESPONDENT /STATE AND NONE FOR  RESPONDENT/VICTIM DESPITE SERVICE OF NOTICE)
This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:

ORDER This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to FIR No. 593/2023 dated 09.08.2023, registered at Police Station- Amarwara District Chhindwara for the offence under Sections 363,366-A, 376(3),376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

He is in detention since 19.02.2024.
2.
A s per the prosecution story, on 09.08.2023, prosecutrix mother lodged report stating that she alongwith her six children use to reside in her parental house.
Her husband is labourer and work at Delhi.

Her daughter whose date of birth is 28.08.2008 and is student of Class-Xth had left home on Kartik @ Ashu @ Kalka Malvya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60816867/
1 07.08.2023 at around 11 A.M. telling that she is going for KYC and will be back by evening.

entities.text: Kartik @ Ashu @ Kalka Malvya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When she did not return in the evening, she thought that she might have gone to her maternal aunt's home.
On 08.08.2023 she made a call to her sister but she informed that prosecutrix has not reached there.
F.I.R was registered.
On 18.02.2024 almost after six months she came back.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed for aforesaid offences.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that prosecutrix in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C has not stated anything against the present applicant.

Therefore,
it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that prosecutrix in her 161 Cr.P.C statement has stated that she was taken away by the present applicant and he had committed rape/ aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.

5 . I have gone through the prosecutrix's statement recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C and other facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pretrial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant- Kartik @ Ashu @ Kalka Malvya be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Kartik @ Ashu @ Kalka Malvya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60816867/
